text: dsh-tinyfish-search 是面向 DeepSeek Harness 的网页搜索插件，通过 ctx.web 注册 tinyfish 提供方，并在 bundle 中把 web_search 路由到 TinyFish Search API。它把查询、可选地区和语言作为请求参数，接收结果后整理为链接、标题、摘要和日期，并按请求上限去重返回。配置支持实时生效，凭据可从 DSH 凭据服务、启动环境或 TINYFISH_API_KEY 读取。适合希望将 Harness 内置网页搜索接入 TinyFish 的用户；需要 TinyFish API key。

dsh-tinyfish-search routes DSH web_search to TinyFish via ctx.web. It sends the query and optional location or language, maps URLs, titles, snippets and dates, removes duplicates, and honors maxResults. It reads live settings and gets its required API key from DSH credentials or TINYFISH_API_KEY.

Route DeepSeek Harness web_search calls to TinyFish Search.

dsh-tinyfish-search 的功能「TinyFish 网页搜索」：将 Harness 的 web_search 接入 TinyFish Search API，并把返回结果映射为统一来源列表。
dsh-tinyfish-search 的功能「地区与语言筛选」：可在配置中填写 location 和 language；每次搜索会把已填写的值作为对应参数传给 TinyFish。
dsh-tinyfish-search 的功能「搜索结果映射」：将返回项转换为统一来源，保留 URL、标题、摘要和发布日期，跳过空 URL 与重复链接，并遵守 maxResults。
dsh-tinyfish-search 的功能「凭据解析」：搜索时按配置读取 API key，可使用 DSH 凭据服务、启动环境或指定环境变量；没有可用密钥时返回缺少凭据错误。
dsh-tinyfish-search 的功能「实时配置」：配置字段以 volatile schema 暴露，插件在每次搜索开始时读取当前值，因此保存的修改无需重新注册 provider。
dsh-tinyfish-search 使用前须知：搜索查询以及已设置的地区和语言会发送到 api.search.tinyfish.ai；请求通过 x-api-key 认证，需配置 TinyFish API key。

dsh-tinyfish-search README · dsh-tinyfish-search：> This project is maintained with the assistance of dsh-superagent.

English | [Chinese](https://github.com/maxwell-feng/dsh-tinyfish-search/blob/main/README.zh.md)

> [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin that backs the built-in `web_search` tool with the [TinyFish Search API](https://docs.tinyfish.ai/search-api). One GET per query, no model call — fast and free (TinyFish Search is free at any wallet balance).

dsh-tinyfish-search README · What it does：DeepSeek Harness's built-in `web_search` tool normally runs through the DeepSeek Anthropic-compatible endpoint (`web-search-deepseek`). This plugin registers an alternative **web search provider** on the `ctx.web` capability seam:

dsh-tinyfish-search README · What it does：- Stable provider id: `tinyfish`
- Every `web_search` call becomes `GET https://api.search.tinyfish.ai?query=...` with the `X-API-Key` header
- `results[]` (title / snippet / url / date) are normalized into the seam's portable source shape
- Reports provider readiness through `WebSearchProvider.ready()` (DeepSeek Harness 0.2.2+): the harness asks it before it declares `web_search`, so a profile with no usable TinyFish credential simply shows no `web_search` tool instead of a tool whose every call fails
- No LLM turn consumed per search — unlike the Anthropic server-tool approach
- Bundled native `icon.svg` vector artwork and bilingual manifest resources (`locale/en.json`, `locale/zh.json`) conforming to DSH 0.2.2-rc.1 display conventions for Plugin Manager
- Pure TypeScript architecture across sources, scripts, and build configurations

dsh-tinyfish-search README · What it does：Installing the bundle **takes over the built-in `web_search` automatically**: the
bundle patch overrides the `web` seam row (`searchProvider: tinyfish`,
`fetchProvider: http` restated), because `dsh-base` pins the seam to
`deepseek-official` and would otherwise keep the tool on the DeepSeek backend.
It also **re-enables the host-level `tool-web` row** (`disabled: false` plus
`search: true`, `fetch: true` and the base timeouts restated): the
`dsh-web-app` bundle ships that row disabled (the Web app normally composes
web tools per agent preset), so without it the model would see no `web_search`
tool at all on a clean web profile install. **Scope note:** re-enabling the
host row makes the tools visible to *every* agent preset on the profile —
including presets that would not otherwise carry web tools (e.g. `minimal`);
a preset that mounts its own `tool-web` row still shadows this global
registration for its agents. To scope the tools to one preset instead,
override or remove the `tool-web` row in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`
and add `tool-web` to that preset's agent composition. Later layers (profile
/ home `cordis.patch.yml` / `--patch`)

dsh-tinyfish-search README · What it does：Configuration is declared as a **volatile schema** (DeepSeek Harness 0.1.7+): the
Host reads the `Config` schema this plugin exports and renders it as the form for
the `dsh-tinyfish-search` row on the Plugins page. There is no plugin-side
settings registration and no plugin-supplied browser half. A saved edit reaches
the next search without a restart.

dsh-tinyfish-search README · Requirements：- DeepSeek Harness `dsh` CLI (any profile with the web seam, e.g. `web`) — the build baseline is `0.2.2-rc.1` (released 2026-11-04 on the npm `next` tag) and the plugin is also verified on `0.2.1-rc.5` (npm `latest`, the desktop runtime); `0.2.2` carries `WebSearchProvider.ready()` while the `0.2.1-rc.*` maintenance line predates it, so a profile on that line runs the plugin without the readiness gate; the plugin declares `engines.dsh` `>=0.1.7-alpha.2 <0.3.0`, so the whole `0.1.7` prerelease line and the `0.2.x` line are admitted
- Node.js `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` (matches the harness engine range) — on a `0.2.2-rc.1` host the effective floor is Node 24.9, because that host raises its own minimum to 24.9 and refuses to run below it; this plugin's `engines.node` is unchanged
- A [TinyFish API key](https://agent.tinyfish.ai/api-keys) (free to create; Search is free)
- The harness credential seam and launch environment (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-credentials`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-launch-environment`) are required peers — every `dsh` profile carries them already

dsh-tinyfish-search README · Harness compatibility gate：DeepSeek Harness verifies a plugin's declared runtime requirement against the
running runtime **before** it admits the row, and refuses an incompatible plugin
instead of loading it. **Since `0.2.1-alpha.4` the rule reads differently:** when
a package declares its own `engines.dsh` range, that range decides alone and the
`@deepseek-ai/dsh*` `peerDependencies` are ignored for the compatibility
judgement; the peers are consulted only as a fallback when `engines.dsh` is
absent. Both are matched with prerelease semantics
(`semver.satisfies(runtime, range, { includePrerelease: true })`), so prerelease
runtimes participate in the comparison, and a refusal record reports
`requirements` rather than `peers`.

dsh-tinyfish-search README · Harness compatibility gate：This plugin declares `engines.dsh: ">=0.1.7-alpha.2 <0.3.0"`, and that range
holds on `0.2.2-rc.1`, on `0.2.1-rc.5`, on `0.2.0-rc.2`, on `0.2.0-rc.1`, and
on the whole `0.1.7` prerelease line — so no exemption is needed. Because
`0.14.0` and `0.13.0` already declared that widened range in `engines.dsh` as
well, they remain admitted on `0.2.2-rc.1` too. The narrow-range `0.12.0`,
however, declared `^0.1.7-alpha.2`, which excludes `0.2.x`, so the harness still
refuses `0.12.0` on `0.2.x`: upgrade to `0.19.0` instead of granting an
exemption. If you run a `dsh` outside the declared range, DSH refuses the row
with a diagnostic naming the exact requirement pair; to accept that risk
explicitly, grant the exempted exact pair it prints:

dsh-tinyfish-search README · Harness compatibility gate：```sh
dsh plugin allow-version dsh-tinyfish-search@0.19.0 --dsh-version <your-dsh-version> --accept-risk
```

dsh-tinyfish-search README · Configure：| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `apiKey` | — | Literal TinyFish API key (secret role; wins over the env var) |
| `apiKeyEnv` | `TINYFISH_API_KEY` | Environment variable carrying the API key |
| `baseURL` | `https://api.search.tinyfish.ai` | TinyFish Search API endpoint base |
| `location` | — | Optional geo location forwarded as TinyFish's `location` (e.g. `US`); blank/unset sends nothing |
| `language` | — | Optional search language forwarded as TinyFish's `language` (e.g. `en`); blank/unset sends nothing |

Inside a session, call `web_search` and check that results carry TinyFish URLs/snippets. The web search settings card in the GUI shows the provider state.

dsh-tinyfish-search README · Usage：After installation, no code changes required. In any session with the `web` profile:

1. The model calls `web_search` as usual (e.g. "search for TinyFish docs").
2. The harness routes it through `ctx.web → tinyfish → https://api.search.tinyfish.ai`.
3. Results appear as `WebSearchSource[]` (`url` / `title` / `snippet` / `publishedAt`) in the tool result.
4. Check GUI: **Settings → Web Search** shows provider `tinyfish` and `available: true` when the API key is configured.

dsh-tinyfish-search README · Usage：Availability, readiness and failure are three different signals. `available()` is a cheap local check the seam uses to pick a provider while an operation runs. `ready()` answers whether a search for a model request on a given chat route has a credential to send, and `dsh-tool-web` uses it as the activation condition of `web_search` — no usable credential, no tool. A search that still runs without a key (for example a programmatic caller that bypasses the gate) fails with `WEB_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_MISSING` rather than reaching TinyFish unauthenticated.

dsh-tinyfish-search README · Usage：Abort and error semantics follow the `dsh-web` seam: `WEB_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_MISSING` when no key, `WEB_ABORTED` on cancellation, `WEB_PROVIDER_ERROR` otherwise.

TinyFish returns no long-form summary and no generated answer, so the plugin fills neither `WebSearchSource.summary` nor `WebSearchResult.content`: both are optional on the seam because not every provider returns them, and inventing a value would make the seam lie.
dsh-tinyfish-search README · Usage：See the [Usage Guide](USAGE.md) for providers, credential configuration, worked examples, and the error table.

dsh-tinyfish-search README · Uninstall：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-tinyfish-search
```

Removes the bundle layer and the `tinyfish` provider registration, and restores
the composed `web` / `tool-web` rows to exactly what the underlying bundles
ship (an inserted row's override returns to the row's own defaults when the
inserting layer is removed). Restart `dsh --profile web` to confirm
`web_search` falls back to the base `deepseek-official` provider (or none if
no other provider is installed).

pnpm install
pnpm build     # tsc -> lib/
pnpm test      # node --test (mocked fetch)
pnpm typecheck # tsc --noEmit, src + test + scripts

The repository is TypeScript throughout; there is no JavaScript source to keep in
sync. The bilingual-documents gate is
[`scripts/check-docs-language.ts`](./scripts/check-docs-language.ts), which CI runs
with bare Node (no dependencies installed) before the install step:

```sh
node scripts/check-docs-language.ts
```
